answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a stake-weighted registry before it may post jobs or claim rewards. If identities are later linked by evidence of collusion, governance slashes their bonds and redistributes the funds to affected users. This makes a Sybil swarm costly: the attacker must buy and immobilize tokens for every persona, and risks losing them all. A karst of cheap accounts may look like a nadir-proof crowd, but the jetty of bonded entry gives honest participants a costly signal to check.
